newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rand Mines tumbles on news offer withdrawn.
newsitem.headline: Rand Mines tumbles on news offer withdrawn.

text.p: Shares in Rand Mines Ltd, a South African mining company in the process of being wound up, tumbled in brisk dealings on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Thursday, on news a possible offer for the firm had been withdrawn.
Dealers said the shares had been drifting lower since the morning, with losses deepening after lunch.
By 1240 GMT shares were off 22 cents or over 35 percent to 40 cents, a fresh year low. Trade was brisk with over 3.1 million shares trading in some 154 deals.
"People are bailing out as they feel now that the deal is no longer on, it is just a matter of unbundling the assets and what then?," said one equity trader.
Rand Mines earlier said it was withdrawing a March 17 cautionary announcement in which the firm had said it had received a proposal which could have included an offer for its ordinary shares.
"Shareholders are advised that this proposal has been withdrawn," the firm said in a statement.
A company spokesman told Reuters the mine had been a holding firm that had now unbundled its assets and so was being wound up.
"It was unbundled last year and there are no assets in the business," he said.
The statement said as a result of the possible offer being withdrawn the winding up of the company would continue.
"A further announcement relating to the winding up of Rand Mines will be published in due course," it said.
